plan.design: Controlled parameter sweeps anchored at 10k / 1080p / common-post. Counts and camera movement are crossed; other axes change separately. This is not a full Cartesian matrix.

methodology.schedule: Sequential batches; fresh native browser document/device per case, rotated engine order each repetition. No concurrent benchmark workloads.
methodology.scene: Shared Render IR geometry/material parameters/initial physical replay. Object motion is deterministic by frame and restored before physical-state checks.
methodology.cpu: Render wall time includes authored motion and actual backend buffer updates. Setup, scene construction, shader warmup and environment prefiltering are outside measurement.
methodology.gpu: Common asynchronous hardware pass timestamps, >=95% coverage; excludes copy-only commands and queue gaps.
methodology.frame: Headless RAF intervals, not display refresh or presentation FPS.
methodology.statistics: Pooled per-frame p50/p95/mean plus each independent repetition; min/max of repetition p95 and CV of repetition means show dispersion. No causal/speed significance claim from a sequential run.
methodology.quality: Canonical images at each matrix cell; exact input/motion audits. Cross-engine pixel differences are descriptive. Unsupported common effects are not silently substituted.

engine.instancing: gpu/cpu-batched use instancing; cpu uses individual main-view draws

three.visibility: native bounds per InstancedMesh or per Mesh

babylon.visibility: native bounds per thin-instance batch or per Mesh

capabilities.limitation: Common effects share enablement, not identical implementations or image quality. Bloom threshold 1, weight .46 and initial scale .25 are recorded; soft knees, blur kernels and mip chains differ. No cross-engine quality winner is inferred.

visualReview.method: Direct inspection of saved native GPU PNGs using view_image. Descriptive visual review, not a cross-engine quality-equivalence gate.

reviewed.observations: Cube arrangement and camera framing correspond across the three images. Engine has a brighter sky, lighter distant shading and visible procedural floor detail. Three has stronger shadow contrast; Babylon has a darker sky and ground. Shadow softness and light falloff differ. Aliasing is visible in the distant cube rows with AA disabled on all engines. No quality winner is established.

Native bloom is visible in all three images. Three has a larger/brighter glow around the lower-left cube highlights; Engine is more restrained, Babylon is intermediate. Native brightness/lighting differences remain. Equal bloom quality or strength is not established by common numeric controls.

The final measured frame shows corresponding displaced cube geometry in all three images, consistent with the audited matrix hashes. No gross missing cube groups are visible. Engine retains lighter distant shading and softer shadows; Three/Babylon have darker high-contrast ground shading. This still does not establish equivalent pixel quality.

canonicalRepeatability.scope: Every decoded RGBA8 channel, same backend/configuration/canonical camera, independent fresh devices; no tolerance. This is repeatability, not cross-engine quality equivalence.

limitations: Controlled sweeps, not the full Cartesian product. Three independent rotated-order repetitions per configuration, on one local AMD GPU.
Headless RAF intervals do not establish displayed FPS; GPU time excludes copy-only commands and queue gaps. Exclusive GPU ownership was not established.
Native PBR, shadows, atmospheric/material detail, tone mapping, bloom kernels and IBL filtering differ. Equal quality and a cross-engine quality winner are not established.
The unbatched control disables main-view instancing; Engine can still cache/batch static shadows. Draw-call counts expose this asymmetry.

The first standard run was intentionally canceled because its authored motion adapter duplicated matrix composition for Engine. Its failed report was preserved and no cases were mixed into this corrected run.
Earlier smoke runs are binding/correctness checks, not performance evidence. Earlier full-native quality/frame-budget failures remain unchanged by this common-effects benchmark.
